To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Netherlands has a safe drinking water supply system that does not use chlorine for any purpose.

the Netherlands provides drinking water without chlorine to its consumers and that this is possible because of the following: • The use of the best available source of water, • The application of a multiple barrier treatment, • The prevention of microbial ingress in the distribution system, • The use of biologically stable materials, • The monitoring of water quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: - The microbiological and toxicological safety of the drinking water production chain, - The development of new methods and techniques for the production and distribution of safe drinking water, - The development and application of new methods and tools to assess the safety of drinking water production chains, - The development, application and validation of methods and tools to prevent microbial growth in the drinking water distribution system, - The development (and validation) of methods and techniques to prevent ingress of contamination in the distribution system,
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no need for chlorination of drinking water in the Netherlands, because the water supply and distribution system is designed in such a way that it is not necessary to use chlorine.
the use of chlorine is not necessary for the provision of microbiologically safe drinking water.

the Dutch approach is based on a holistic approach to drinking water quality, in which the focus is not on the use of a single disinfectant, but on a combination of measures that prevent microbial contamination of the drinking water supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide safe drinking-water without the use of any chemical disinfection.
the Dutch drinking water supply system is a very good example of a system that provides a safe drinking water supply without chlorine.
the Dutch approach to drinking water quality is based on the use of the best source available and a preferred treatment process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of chlorine in water treatment is a choice, not a necessity, which should be based on the quality of the water sources, treatment processes, and distribution networks.
the Dutch approach is not only possible but also very effective.

we have shown that it is feasible to provide microbiologically safe drinking water without the addition of chlorine, even if the source is not microbiologically safe, and even if the water is distributed in a large distribution network.
